references.text: God confirms with an oath that Abraham did not spare his only son – a direct follow-up to verse 12 using the same language about not withholding his son.
By faith, Abraham offered up Isaac when he was tested. The book of Hebrews interprets Abraham's action as an expression of deep trust in God's promises.
James uses Abraham's offering of Isaac as proof that faith is demonstrated through deeds – Abraham was justified by what he did.
'He who did not spare his own Son' – Paul uses the same language as Genesis 22:12 and highlights the theological parallel between Abraham's sacrifice and God's giving of His Son.
Joseph says, 'I fear God' – the same expression (ירא אלהים) that the angel uses about Abraham in Genesis 22:12.
God tested Israel in the wilderness to know what was in their hearts – a parallel to God's testing of Abraham to demonstrate his reverence for God.
Proverbs gives the general warning, while Genesis 22 provides the definitive definition of 'fear of God' as total obedience even when it costs one's only son.
A theological parallel concerning God's claim on the firstborn: Exodus shows judgment upon Egypt, while Genesis presents a test of faith that ends with God's own provision.
Contrast in the use of 'not spare': Deuteronomy demands harshness toward a false prophet, whereas Genesis tests whether Abraham can surrender his son to God.
A contrast between Jacob's fear of losing his only son (Gen 42) and Abraham's willingness to offer up his only son (Gen 22), illuminating the theme of 'only son' and fatherly love.
